previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with type 1 diabetes, depression, and alcohol use disorder, was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis triggered by an abdominal abscess and missed insulin doses. She presented with nausea, vomiting, and severe hyperglycemia. In the ED, she received IV fluids, insulin, and antibiotics, and underwent incision and drainage of the abscess. Her DKA resolved with treatment, and renal function normalized. The wound showed clinical improvement with adequate drainage, and she was transitioned to oral antibiotics. A diabetes educator reinforced proper injection techniques, which the patient demonstrated correctly. She was discharged home with a visiting nurse for wound care, adjusted insulin regimen, and follow-up plans for primary care and diabetes management.

___ with history of DM1 and EtOH abuse, recurrent for DKA now

# Diabetic Ketoacidosis: 
# Diabetes Mellitus Type I: Poorly controlled and complicated, 
Last A1C 13%, complicated by recurrent DKA and gastroparesis 
DKA on admission most likely related to medication 
non-compliance. Patient did not follow up with ___ as 
scheduled and reported skipping several Lantus doses because she 
was not feeling well. No fevers or localizing signs of 
infection. Infectious work-up including CXR, UA, urine cx, BCx 
all negative. Prior abscess site well healed without underlying 
fluctuance. Admitted to the ICU for management of DKA nad 
insulin drip. Intial EKG with peaked T Waves consistent with 
hyperkalemia though this resolved with treatment. Anion gap 37 
with glucose of 1019 and PH 6.9 in the ED. LFTs, lipase 
unremarkable. Fingersticks q1hr trended with Chem10 amd VBG 
q2-3hrs during intial course as gap closed. Insulin gtt until 
anion gap closes and FSG < 250, at which point switched to SC 
insulin and continue gtt for one hour overlap. Continued 
aggressive fluid resuscitation with 2 additional 1LNS boluses 
while in ICU, followed by NS + 20K+ at 250cc/hr after FSG<250. 
___ consulted in house and Lantus dosing adjusted, had 
several hypogylcemic episodes prior to discharge so Lantus dose 
reduced. She was seen by ___ nurse educator prior to ___ and 
has follow up with ___ less than a week post-discharge.
  
# Leukocytosis: 
On admission, most likely stress response due to DKA. Infectious 
work-up as above was negative. Resolved on hospital day #2.
  
# Leukopenia
# Neutropenia
Day prior to admission WBC nadirred to mid 2s with 35% and ANC 
count of 900 consistent with moderate Neutropenia. She was put 
on neutropenic precautions and had no fevers during admission or 
infections evident. No clear precipitant for leukopenia was 
found and no definite medications as culprit. Her leukopenia 
improved by morning of discharge and she was no longer 
neutropenic. Etiology remains elusive, however interestingly, 
pattern is identical to last admission; admitted with profound 
leukocytosis in setting of DKA and infection though after 
resolution of DKA WBCs nadir to low 2s then subsequently 
rebounded. She has a similar pattern on review of CBCs dating 
back to ___. Worth full eval in the outpatient setting.
      
# Hyperkalemia: Patient initially total body potassium depleted 
despite hyperkalmeia. Initially with peak t waves on EKG which 
normalized on subsequent monitoring. Hyperkalemia resolved on 
hospital day #2.
   
# Acute Renal Failure: 
On admission. Baseline creatinine 0.5-0.6, presented with 
creatinine 1.9 in the setting of severe volume depletion from 
DKA (BUN:Cr > 20). Resolved on hospital day #2. 
    
# EtOH Use: 
Per patient prior history of heavy alchol use. Denies drinking 
for the past one month. Monitored for signs of alcohol 
withdrawal, started on MVI/thiamine/folate. Social work 
consulted.
    
# Depression: 
Continued mirtazapine and effexor.
